censoring_policy: all planned trials remain in denominator; no qualifying success (including evidence issues) is capped at timeout, never zero

policy.arbitrary_intersection: either distinct real branch; no invented choice for unnamed terms
policy.assert_in_polygon: closed interior of a strictly convex polygon
policy.assert_on_segment: closed segment, without upstream's artificial 20% inset
policy.closed: nonnegative margin; small negative margins are unresolved, never passed
policy.line_comparison: angle and local construction-anchor incidence; unanchored free lines use chart origin
policy.local_scales: construction feature lengths reused by incidence; not all-point diameter
policy.minor_arc: strict minor arc; coincident or antipodal endpoints unresolved/invalid
policy.nonintersecting_figures: failed or unresolved near numerical boundary; never fake points
policy.normalization: first distinct declared point pair; otherwise first positive circle radius
policy.param_in_polygon: strict interior of a strictly convex polygon
policy.polygon: strictly convex polygon in the declared cyclic order, either orientation
policy.scalar_measurements: length/area literals retain the original witness units
policy.strict: positive margin > tolerance; positive smaller margin is unresolved

interpretation: numerical configuration validation only; neither existence proof, theorem proof, enumeration completeness nor a literal replication of all 39 paper instances

resource_scope.three_seed_inference: descriptive only; no population-rate or speed-superiority proof

scope_exceptions.IMO_2010_P2: User approved 0 < tf < 1; exclude original endpoint configurations on both sides (2026-08-31)
scope_exceptions.IMO_2014_P4: Both inputs already use interior points P,Q; do not claim coverage of original closed-side boundary configurations

sensitivity_warning: tolerances affect both equality error and boundary/branch resolution; success sets need not be nested
timing_policy: first native-accepted model atomically emitted within limit and passing the offline checker; timeout/crash later is a separate outcome
